note: Fallbacks approved by name. Each one was shown to David as its own question, never buried in a plan. An empty list is the normal state for a project.

withdrawn.why: These two searched for a helper script and moved on when a location came up empty. That was the wrong answer. A missing core tool means the project's install is broken — the fix is to REPAIR it and continue with every tool present, not to route around the gap. Routing around it is what let binvoice run for weeks with 20 of 38 tools while every update reported success. Superseded by M108 (bin/gsd-t-install-check.cjs + the SessionStart repair hook).

fallbacks.whatFails: Reading the end of the conversation transcript fails if the file is mid-write, rotated, or briefly locked.
fallbacks.howLikely: Occasional — the transcript is written continuously while this hook runs.
fallbacks.whyNotHalt: This governs how a reply READS, never whether it is true. Blocking a correct answer because a log file was momentarily unreadable would be a worse outcome than showing a long reply. Nothing is fabricated: an empty read means the reply passes through exactly as written.
fallbacks.whatItDoesInstead: Returns nothing read, so the hook allows the original reply through untouched.

fallbacks.whatFails: The concise settings file exists but is not valid JSON.
fallbacks.whyNotHalt: Same reasoning as the transcript read. The safe direction here is to rewrite with defaults, which can only shorten a reply, never lose content — every rewrite is separately checked for lost questions, warnings, paths and code blocks, and rejected if anything went missing.

fallbacks.whatFails: Checking whether the transcript path is a regular file.
fallbacks.whyNotHalt: Part of the same transcript read approved above; it is a precondition check, not a recovery.
fallbacks.whatItDoesInstead: Treats a non-file as nothing to read, so the reply passes through untouched.
